result:
Compilation succeeded. Summary of what was done:

- Wrote `tests/org/apache/commons/lang3/BitFieldAgentTest.java` (JUnit 5 / Jupiter, matching the jars in `lib/`), self-contained, covering all 25 documented methods plus both constructors.
- Grounded expectations in the documented formulas (clear = `holder & ~mask`, set = `holder | mask`, raw = `holder & mask`, isSet/isAllSet definitions) and in the class-level Javadoc's own worked paint-mixing example for the shift-dependent `getValue`/`setValue`/`getShortValue`/`setShortValue` methods.
- Covered boundary cases: zero mask (vacuous `isAllSet` true, `isSet` always false), all-bits mask (`-1`/`-1L`), negative byte/short widening through sign extension, value truncation when `setValue`/`setShortValue` receives a value wider than the field, and a long mask reaching bits beyond the 32-bit range (only expressible via the new `BitField(long)` constructor).
- Before compiling, I cross-checked every hardcoded numeric expectation against independent arithmetic and caught 4 mistakes in my own hex math (`clearLongClearsOnlyMaskedBits`, both `getRawValue` tests, and one `set(int)` case) and corrected them.

`./compile.sh` now reports `compiled OK`.
